verification.note: Profile read: 'Ned Blackhawk (Western Shoshone) is a Professor of History at Yale'. Identity statement only.

row.context: Munsee Delaware historian of Indigenous women's work and of Indian Affairs archives as sites of possibility and contestation for Indigenous historians (2014, 2018).
row.works: 'Indigenous People, Archives and History' (2018); Indigenous Women, Work, and History (2014)

row.context: Cree historian (Fisher River Cree Nation) of Cree intellectual traditions and of the academy's treatment of Indigenous history (1998, 2010).
row.works: Cree Intellectual Traditions in History (2010); Reflections on the Social Relations of Indigenous Oral History (2005, unread; cited by Leddy 2010)

row.context: Métis historian whose One of the Family (2010) reads a northwestern Métis community through wahkootowin, in her own framing.
row.works: One of the Family (2010); 'Ways of Knowing' (2018)

row.context: Cowessess First Nation historian of kinship and treaty land (2013) and critic of how historians have written the 1880s starvation policy (2018).
row.works: 'Historians and Indigenous Genocide in Saskatchewan' (2018); Elder Brother and the Law of the People (2013)

row.context: Anishinabe kwe historian of her own Serpent River First Nation (2010).
Narrator-author of Life Lived Like a Story (1990), as the book credits her; Tagish and Tlingit.
row.works: Life Lived Like a Story, collaborative volume (1990)

row.context: Narrator-author of Life Lived Like a Story (1990), as the book credits her; Southern Tutchone and Tlingit.
row.works: Life Lived Like a Story, collaborative volume (1990)

row.context: Narrator-author of Life Lived Like a Story (1990), as the book credits her; Southern Tutchone.
row.works: Life Lived Like a Story, collaborative volume (1990)

row.context: Opaskwayak Cree scholar of Indigenous research methodology: Research Is Ceremony (2008).
Citizen of the Red Cliff Band of Lake Superior Ojibwe; An Infinity of Nations (2012) writes the Great Lakes from the Anishinaabe world.
Western Shoshone historian of the Great Basin (2006) and of Indigenous absence in American history (2023).
row.works: Violence over the Land (2006); The Rediscovery of America (2023)
